key_insight: Halide ordering strongly reshapes phase stability in mixed-halide perovskites, shifting structural transition temperatures by up to 100 K and explaining non-linear composition trends.
engineering_relevance: For solar-cell design, controlling halide and A-site composition can be used to tune phase stability, miscibility, and operational robustness under device-relevant temperatures.
method: Trained machine-learned interatomic potentials on DFT reference data for mixed Cs/Rb lead halide perovskites.
Used hybrid Monte Carlo-molecular dynamics to sample both configurational and vibrational degrees of freedom at scale.
Mapped miscibility gaps and halide ordering across Br-Cl, Br-I, and Cl-I systems over 200-500 K.
evidence_signal: Large-scale simulations reproduced miscibility gaps in all three binary halide systems and showed that halide ordering correlates with experimentally observed non-linear phase-boundary behavior.
watch_item: The conclusions rely on MLIP fidelity to DFT and simulated composition/temperature ranges, so transferability to all processing conditions and defect-rich devices may be limited.
paper_title: Strong Impact of Halide Ordering on Structural Phase Transitions in Mixed Perovskites
